title: Browser cannot access localhost:8000
scenario: Compose startup finishes, but the learner's browser cannot connect to http://localhost:8000. The responsible layer is not disclosed.
knownFacts: docker compose up -d completed
The browser reports that localhost:8000 cannot be reached
Command evidence can isolate one concrete layer
hints: Separate host port from container port; inspect resolved Compose configuration.
Find the port the application process actually listens on inside the container.
Compare the 8000:8000 mapping with a process listening on 8001.
solution: The Backend process listens on container port 8001 while Compose publishes host 8000 to container 8000. Align the Compose target/health contract with 8001, then verify with compose config, ps, ss or logs, curl, and caller regression.

title: Portal/API request fails across multiple layers
scenario: The Portal cannot complete a create request. Containers exist, but the UI only reports a generic failure. Port, DNS, environment, database, migration, and proxy remain possible until evidence excludes them.
knownFacts: The stack was rebuilt from source
The failure crosses Browser, proxy, Backend, and PostgreSQL boundaries
No destructive volume command is allowed during diagnosis
hints: Create a layer-by-layer evidence table from external URL to database readiness.
Compare the Backend DATABASE_URL hostname and migration state with Compose service names.
The Backend uses localhost for PostgreSQL and has not applied the current migration.
solution: The Backend container uses localhost in DATABASE_URL, so it targets itself instead of the postgres service; after correcting the service hostname, the current migration must also be applied. Verify DNS, pg_isready, migration status, API response, proxy route, and persistence regression.

title: Login succeeds but protected API returns 403
scenario: A demo user completes login and receives a token, yet the protected purchase endpoint returns 403. Do not disable the Backend guard or grant broad roles.
knownFacts: OIDC login succeeds
The API validates the token enough to distinguish it from 401
The expected role must be enforced by Backend
hints: Treat 403 as an authorization path after token validity.
Decode the token and compare role claims with mapper and Backend guard expectations.
The user has the realm role, but the client mapper omits it from the claim read by Backend.
solution: The Keycloak client mapper does not place the assigned role in the token claim expected by the Backend guard. Correct the mapper/claim contract, issue a fresh token, and verify 403 for the wrong role plus 200 for the allowed role.

title: Workflow executes twice and creates a duplicate action
scenario: One business event produces two purchase actions after a webhook retry. The system must remain retry-safe without deleting audit history.
knownFacts: Both workflow executions have the same business event
The first HTTP response was slow
A write endpoint accepted both calls
hints: Compare business ID, correlation ID, and idempotency key across both executions.
A retry is normal; duplicate side effects indicate a missing contract.
The caller retries without a stable idempotency key and the Backend does not enforce uniqueness.
solution: The retry reused the business event but no stable idempotency key was sent or enforced, so the Backend created two actions. Define a stable key, enforce uniqueness server-side, return the original result on retry, and regression-test concurrent duplicates.

title: System is running but dashboard data is wrong
scenario: A transaction succeeds and services remain healthy, but the dashboard total is wrong. Diagnose data correctness without giving Metabase write access.
knownFacts: The transaction API returned success
Metabase can connect
Service health alone cannot prove KPI correctness
hints: Trace one business ID from source rows to the KPI query.
Compare dashboard filters/timezone with a direct read-only SQL result.
The dashboard applies an old status filter that excludes the new completed state.
solution: The KPI question uses a stale status filter and excludes the new completed transaction state. Verify source rows and row counts with read-only SQL, correct the filter, compare totals, and regression-test other KPI cards and timezone boundaries.

title: RAG returns 500; infrastructure root cause unknown
scenario: The RAG endpoint returns 500. Qdrant, collection configuration, Ollama, model availability, service URLs, and resources remain possible until evidence narrows the chain.
knownFacts: The RAG service process is running
The error appears only when generating an answer
SV1 must hand off if infrastructure passes and answer quality is the issue
hints: Check dependencies independently before changing prompt or retrieval logic.
Ollama health and required-model availability are different checks.
Ollama is reachable, but the configured model is absent from the model list.
solution: The Ollama service is reachable but the configured model has not been pulled. Confirm model list and storage, pull the pinned model, retry the RAG request, then restart and verify model persistence plus Qdrant dependency regression.

title: Agent attempts an unauthorized sensitive action
scenario: A Sales user asks the Agent to approve its own purchase request. The Agent proposes a write tool call. Preserve audit evidence and prevent privilege escalation.
knownFacts: The user has a valid Sales token
Write tools may only create DRAFT/PENDING records
There is no approved direct-approve tool
hints: Authorization belongs to the Backend, not to prompt wording.
Inspect requested tool, actor role, target status, and audit record.
The tool schema accepts status=APPROVED and the Backend endpoint fails to overwrite it to PENDING.
solution: The write schema accepts a caller-controlled approved status and the Backend does not force DRAFT/PENDING. Reject the argument, enforce status server-side, keep approval in a Manager HITL endpoint, audit the denial, and regression-test wrong role, huge quantity, duplicate, and self-approve cases.

title: Unknown incident during release rehearsal
scenario: During a timed fresh-machine rehearsal, the main flow fails after configuration and startup. The failing layer is intentionally undisclosed. Use the frozen inventory and evidence protocol; do not edit source or delete volumes.
knownFacts: The same release artifact passed on another machine
All required containers appear in compose ps
The failure started after configuration was copied to the fresh machine
hints: Compare frozen configuration and resolved Compose output between machines.
A container can be running while a dependency contract is wrong.
The fresh machine uses an old OLLAMA_MODEL value that is not present in the release model manifest.
solution: Configuration drift set OLLAMA_MODEL to an older model absent from the release manifest. Restore the frozen environment contract, bootstrap the pinned model, verify RAG/Agent and main E2E, then add a configuration validation/smoke guard and rerun release regression.
